latest_release.name: v5.1.0
latest_release.body:
The persist and devtools middleware are improved thanks to @Tnalxmsk and @dgesteves!

## Release note

- The `persist` middleware now supports `PromiseLike` results from storage reads, migrations, and migration writes. `persist.rehydrate()` now returns a native `Promise<void>`, which you can await to ensure hydration is complete.
- The `devtools` middleware now supports dispatching store actions directly from Redux DevTools using the new `actionCreators` option. It also supports nested actions and arguments.

## What's Changed
* fix(middleware): persist migration supporting promise-like by @dai-shi in https://github.com/pmndrs/zustand/pull/3583
* fix(middleware): devtools action dispatching by @dai-shi in https://github.com/pmndrs/zustand/pull/3595


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/pmndrs/zustand/compare/v5.0.16...v5.1.0

A small, fast and scalable bearbones state-management solution using simplified flux principles. Has a comfy API based on hooks, isn't boilerplatey or opinionated. Don't disregard it because it's cute. It has quite the claws, lots of time was spent dealing with common pitfalls, like the dreaded [zombie child problem](https://react-redux.js.org/api/hooks#stale-props-and-zombie-children), [react concurrency](https://github.com/bvaughn/rfcs/blob/useMutableSource/text/0000-use-mutable-source.md), and [context loss](https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/13332) between mixed renderers. It may be the one state-manager in the React space that gets all of these right. You can try a live [demo](https://zustand-demo.pmnd.rs/) and read the [docs](https://zustand.docs.pmnd.rs/). ```bash npm install zustand ``` :warning: This readme is written for JavaScript users. If you are a TypeScript user, be sure to check out our [TypeScript Usage section](#typescript-usage). ## First create a store Your store is a hook! You can put anything in it: primitives, objects, functions. State has to be updated immutably and the `set` function [merges state](./docs/learn/guides/immutable-state-and-merging.md) to help it. ```jsx import { create } from 'zustand' const useBearStore = create((set) => ({ bears: 0, increasePopulation: () => set((state) => ({ bears: state.bears + 1 })), removeAllBears: () => set({ bears: 0 }), })) ``` ## Then bind your components, and that's it! Use the hook anywhere, no providers are needed.
